 ORDER

The petitioners are seeking issuance of writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to issue final notification and to consider the representations of the petitioners dated 18.03.2024 submitted to the respondents vide Annexures-E & E1, F & F1, G & G1, H, J & J1, K & K1 and L.
2.

Heard Smt.Vidyavati M.Kotturshettar, learned counsel for the petitioners, Smt.Kirtilata R.Patil,
learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent Nos.1 to 4, 6 & 7 and Sri Chetan Munnoli,
learned counsel for respondent No.5 3.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, the petitioners are the owners of the land.

The respondents intending to acquire the land for UKP project issued notification under Section 11(1) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, NC: 2024:KHC-D:6432 Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 ("the Act, 2013"
for short) as per Annexure-A on 31.03.2015.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, NC: 2024:KHC-D:6432 Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Pursuant to the notification, the name of the respondents came to be entered in the record of rights, restraining the petitioners from creating any third party rights.
However, no further steps are taken and no final notification was issued.
Thereafter, one more notification was issued on 07.10.2022 as per Annexure-B.
Even thereafter, no further steps were taken.

As a result of which,
the petitioners are debarred from entering into the property.
The respondents are not issuing the final notification nor passing the award to enable the petitioners to claim compensation.
As per Section 25 of the Act 2013, the period within which the award is to be made is 12 months from the date of publication of the declaration under Section 19 of the Act, 2013.
If no award is made within that period, the entire proceedings for acquisition of the land shall lapse.

4. Learned counsel submitted that, the first proviso to Section 25 of the Act, 2013 enables the NC:
2024:KHC-D:6432 appropriate Government to extend the period of 12 months, if in its opinion circumstances exist justifying the same.
But as per the second proviso decision to extent the period shall be recorded in writing, the same shall be notified and shall be uploaded in the Website of the authorities concerned.
But no such extension is made in the present case.

Therefore prays for Annappa S/O Dundappa Balamatti Urf ... vs The Secretary on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104885647/

sentences.text: 5. Learned High Court Government Pleader while admitting the facts narrated in the petition submitted that there is delay in issuing the final notification and passing of the award.
However, if reasonable time is granted, final notification will be issued, award will be passed and compensation will be paid, in accordance with law.
Accordingly, she prays for passing appropriate order.
6. It is not in dispute that the petitioners are the owners of the land which was notified for acquisition for Upper Krishna project.
Notification produced as per Annexure-A under Section 11 of the Act, 2013 was passed on 31.03.2015.
It is also not in dispute that final NC: 2024:KHC-D:6432 notification was not issued and the award is also not passed till today.

As per Section 19 of the Act,
2013 after publication of declaration and summary of rehabilitation and settlement, when the property is required for public purpose, the final notification is to be published as per Section 25 of the Act, 2013.
The Collector shall make an award within a period of 12 months from the date of such publication of declaration under Section 19 of the Act, 2013.
If no such award is made within a period of 12 months, the entire proceedings for acquisition of the land shall lapse.

Even though the Government is authorised to extend the period of 12 months as per the proviso to Section 25 of the Act, 2013, such extension shall be in writing and shall be notified and to be uploaded on the website of the authority concerned.
But it is not the contention taken by the respondents that there was any extension of period.

There cannot be any justification for the respondents for not issuing the final notification and not passing the award, when the notification under Section 11 of the Act, 2013 was published on 31.03.2015.
However, the petitioners are not seeking the declaration that the entire proceedings for acquisition of the land has already lapsed.
The prayer is for issuance of writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents to pass award forthwith and to pay reasonable compensation.
7. The materials on record also disclose that the petitioners have submitted various representations to all the respondents, but it has not given any relief to the petitioners.
Therefore I am of the opinion that the petitioners are entitled for the relief as claimed.
Hence, the petition is liable to be allowed.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The writ petition is allowed.

Respondent Nos.4, 6 and 7 are directed to issue final notification within three months from the date of receipt of copy of this order and pass award determining the reasonable compensation payable to the petitioners in accordance with law, within three months from NC: 2024:KHC-D:6432 the date of issuing the final notification.
Failing which, the petitioners are entitled to take further action in the matter.
